title: Flash Lite's 503 sends the rater call to Flash, and the spend log records both attempts
subtitle: Example: a made-up timeline with the real rules. The rater has a 2 s budget, and both models are enabled.

outcome.title: Answered by Flash, at about 4× the price
lines: $0.000735 instead of $0.00018 on Flash Lite. The feature never saw the outage. One GROUP BY over feature, user or model shows the ×4.

captions.title: Check who pays, before any network call
captions.text: The rater's call names user 42 (example) and the feature `onboarding_level_chat`. A call without a payer is refused on the spot.

captions.title: Build the list of models to try
captions.text: The named model goes first, then every other enabled model by priority: [Flash Lite, Flash].

captions.title: Retry only what a retry can fix, inside the budget
captions.text: Flash Lite answers 503. A second try would come after 3 s, which does not fit the 2 s budget, so the gateway gives up on Flash Lite.

captions.title: Write down the failure too
captions.text: The failed attempt reports no tokens. It is still recorded, as a zero-token row marked as an error.

captions.title: Fall back to the next model
captions.text: Flash gets a fresh 2 s budget and answers at 1.1 s. The feature never sees the outage, but its answer now comes from a different model.

captions.title: Price the attempt the moment it happens
captions.text: The rows are priced at today's rates and written in the background while the answer goes back. One `GROUP BY` over feature, user or model then shows the ×4.
